Three versions are ready. They all contain the **same six bookmarks** (about space, programming, and cooking) — only the way you organise differs. Please open them one at a time and, in each, do the small action I describe:

**Option A — Folders:** http://maker:4001/organise-folders.html
Each bookmark sits in exactly one folder. **Click "Recipes" on the left** to narrow to just those, then **use the "Folder" dropdown on a card to move it** to another folder. Notice a bookmark can only be in one place at a time.

**Option B — Tags:** http://maker:4001/organise-tags.html
A bookmark can carry several labels. **Tap "#to-read" at the top** to see everything you've marked to read — across all topics — then **tap "#python" as well** to narrow further. Try **"+ label"** on a card to add your own.

**Option C — Automatic:** http://maker:4001/organise-auto.html
You file nothing by hand; bookmarks group themselves by website. **Just scroll** and see them gathered under nasa.gov, realpython.com, and so on.

These represent three real philosophies: **one tidy home per link (A)**, **flexible cross-cutting labels (B)**, or **zero manual effort (C)**. There's no right answer — I want the one that matches how *you* naturally reach for a saved link.

Which one feels most like how you'd want to organise — or is it some blend? Tell me what clicks and what doesn't, and I'll fold it into our main prototype.
